reason: General flashes reached 4 per second in a 341x256 px window at frames 0-598; WCAG 2.3.1 allows at most 3.

fixes.rationale: Slows the strobe from 4 cycles per second to 1, so it can produce at most 1 flash per second.
Keeps the rhythm but holds both states above 0.80 relative luminance, so no transition counts as a general flash.
Shrinks the box below 25% of a 341 x 256 px window, so its flashes no longer meet the area rule.

evidenceFrames.label: Frame just before that flash event
First qualifying general flash of violation 1

limitations: Headless sRGB rendering is not a physical display; brightness, gamma and viewing distance differ per user.
Canvas/WebGL attribution is element-level only (what is drawn inside cannot be attributed).
Cross-origin iframes are unattributable and cannot be clock-controlled.
Animated GIF/WebP/APNG force non-deterministic capture (strategy C) and a PASS becomes INCONCLUSIVE.
The fine-pattern exception (T6) and spatial-pattern hazards are not evaluated.
Only the captured viewport and duration are analysed; content revealed by scrolling or interaction is analysed only if an interaction script drives it.
Window size for viewports other than 1024 px wide is scaled by the width ratio (an assumption).
No numbers in this repository are estimates: accuracy, agreement and runtime figures exist only in docs/RESULTS.md, produced by flashtrace bench, with date and commit hash.
assumptions: TEST FIXTURE: frames are synthetic NumPy images, not a browser capture.
Frame i is at i / 60 s of animation time.
The 341 x 256 px window corresponds to a 1024 px wide viewport viewed at a typical distance.
Red flashes use the WCAG 2.2 red-flash definition (redRule wcag22).
disclaimer: Analysis aid, not a compliance certification.
